title: A Sixth AI Editor Now Reviews Every Explainer Script | vitalii.no
description:
The first fully-rendered explainer film exposed real problems no single prompt had caught: the script quizzed the viewer mid-video with predict-and-recall questions, it never actually spoke to the specific child who had asked, numbers came out vague or abbreviated instead of exact, and the core mechanism behind the answer could get buried under filler instead of taking up a real share of the runtime.

I added a sixth agent to the scripting pipeline — a literary editor running as a second AI pass, thinking in Ukrainian and writing the target language from the meaning rather than translating line by line. New rules now hard-block any predict, check, recall, or reveal-the-answer beat, allow a question mark only in the opening and one closing beat, and feed every agent the actual asker's name, grade, and age so the language and depth genuinely fit them. Every script now also requires real numbers with real sources instead of rounded guesses.

Result: the core-mechanism beats that explain the actual answer must now fill at least 30 percent of the video's runtime in dedicated full-screen diagrams, instead of competing with filler for space.
